#Principal paper
##Table 1. Descriptive characteristics of the study sample
```{r echo=F}
library(flextable)
flextable::set_flextable_defaults(font.family = "Arial", font.size = 7, layout = "autofit",border.color = "black",split = T, padding = 2, test.align = "center")
t1 <- read_excel("C:/Users/Beatr/Desktop/Profith/Agueda/Proyectos_R/Acc_script/processed_data/table1.xlsx")
##t1= flextable(t1)
t1 = flextable::as_flextable(t1,show_coltype = F, max_row = 40)
t1 = align(t1,align ="center", part = "all")
t1 <- align(t1, align = "left", part = "body", j = 1)

t1 = set_header_labels(t1,rn ="", Overall = "Mean ± SD",  `0` = "Lower levels",  `1`= "Higher levels",   `0.1` = "Lower levels",  `1.1`= "Higher levels")
t1 = add_footer_lines(t1 ,"Abbreviations: acc, accuracy; AD,Alzheimer’s disease; CL, centiloid; n, number; y, years; SD, standard deviation; sec, seconds; min, minutes; cm, centimeters; m, meters; rt, reaction time; ilr,isometric log-ratio coordinate. ")
t1 <- padding(t1, i=c(1,3:11,13:15,17:21,23:24,26:29), j=1, padding.left=20) ##i=Variable and j=Colum
t1 <- bold(t1, i = c(2,12, 16, 22,25 ), j = 1) ##Negrita words
set_caption(t1, caption = "")
```

##Figure 2.Linear regression models showing the associations of movement behaviors with cognitive domains and Alzheimer's disease brain signatures.
```{r echo=FALSE,fig.height=5, fig.width=9, fig.align="center"} 
#| echo: false 
#| fig-cap: "Linear regression models showing the associations of movement behaviors (using a compositional analysis approach) with cognitive domains and Alzheimer's disease brain signatures. For each behavior, independent models were constructed. Models for cognitive domains were adjusted for sex, age, and education level, whereas models for Alzheimer's disease brain signatures were adjusted for sex and education level only. In all models, the isometric log-ratio coordinates of the movement behaviors were included as predictor variables. The table reports the results for the coordinate of the dominant behavior relative to the other behaviors. β: Unstandardized beta coefficients indicate how much the outcome changes for a one-unit increase in the respective isometric log-ratio coordinate. This reflects a proportional increase in the dominant behavior relative to the rest of behaviors. "

knitr::include_graphics( "C:/Users/Beatr/Desktop/Profith/Agueda/Proyectos_R/Acc_script/processed_data/fig2_all.png")
```

#Supplementary material
##Table S1. ANOVA F-tests for the association between 24-hour movement behavior composition and cognitive performance, and moderation by AD brain signatures

```{r echo=F}
library(readxl)
library(flextable)
library(dplyr)
library(officer)

flextable::set_flextable_defaults(
  font.family = "Arial",
  font.size = 9,
  layout = "fixed",
  border.color = "black",
  split = TRUE,
  padding = 1,
  text.align = "center"
)

t1 <- read_excel("C:/Users/Beatr/Desktop/Profith/Agueda/Proyectos_R/Acc_script/processed_data/table_anova.xlsx")

# Si el Excel ya tiene filas de encabezado dentro de la tabla, eliminarlas
# Esto elimina filas tipo "Variable / Episodic memory..." y la fila "F / P"
t1 <- t1 %>%
  filter(
    !Variable %in% c("Variable", "", NA)
  )

# Acortar nombres de columnas para trabajar más fácil
names(t1) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Attention_F", "Attention_P",
  "Episodic_F", "Episodic_P",
  "Processing_F", "Processing_P",
  "Visuospatial_F", "Visuospatial_P",
  "Working_F", "Working_P"
  
)

t1 <- flextable(t1)

t1 <- align(t1, align = "center", part = "all")
t1 <- align(t1, align = "left", part = "body", j = 1)

t1 <- set_header_labels(
  t1,
  Variable = "Variable",
  `Attentional/inhibitory control_F` = "F",
  `Attentional/inhibitory control_P` = "P",
  `Episodic memory_F` = "F",
  `Episodic memory_P` = "P",
  `Processing speed_F` = "F",
  `Processing speed_P` = "P",
  `Visuospatial processing_F` = "F",
  `Visuospatial processing_P` = "P",
  `Working memory_F` = "F",
  `Working memory_P` = "P"
)

t1 <- add_header_row(
  t1,
  values = c(
    "",
    "Attention/\ninhibition",
    "Episodic\nmemory",
    "Processing\nspeed",
    "Visuospatial\nprocessing",
    "Working\nmemory"
  ),
  colwidths = c(1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2)
)

# Anchos compactos pero legibles
t1 <- width(t1, j = 1, width = 1.80)
t1 <- width(t1, j = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10), width = 0.46) # F
t1 <- width(t1, j = c(3, 5, 7, 9, 11), width = 0.50) # P

# Fuente más grande
t1 <- fontsize(t1, size = 9, part = "body")
t1 <- fontsize(t1, size = 8.5, part = "header")
t1 <- fontsize(t1, size = 7.5, part = "footer")

# Compactar sin hacerlo minúsculo
t1 <- padding(t1, padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1, padding.left = 1, padding.right = 1, part = "all")

# Formato
t1 <- bold(t1, j = 1, part = "body")
t1 <- bold(t1, part = "header")
t1 <- align(t1, align = "center", part = "header")
t1 <- align(t1, align = "left", part = "footer")

t1 <- add_footer_lines(
  t1,
  "ANOVA F-test from linear regression model comparisons investigating associations between overall 24-hour movement behavior composition and each cognitive domain, and whether these associations were moderated by Alzheimer’s disease brain signatures. The 24-hour movement behavior composition was represented by three isometric log-ratio coordinates. Moderation was tested by comparing models with and without the three ILR × moderator interaction terms. GMMD and thickness/volume signatures were tested in separate models. Abbreviations: F, F statistic; P, P-value; GMMD, gray matter mean diffusivity; Attention/inhibition, attentional/inhibitory control."
)

t1 <- fontsize(t1, size = 7.5, part = "footer")
t1 <- align(t1, align = "left", part = "footer")

set_caption(t1, caption = "")
```

##Table S2. Linear regression models showing the associations of movement behaviors with cognitive domains and Alzheimer's disease brain signatures moderated by AD brain signatures.

```{r echo=F}
library(flextable)
flextable::set_flextable_defaults(font.family = "Arial", font.size = 7, layout = "autofit",border.color = "black",split = T, padding = 2, test.align = "center")
t1 <- read_excel("C:/Users/Beatr/Desktop/Profith/Agueda/Proyectos_R/Acc_script/processed_data/table_interaction_brain.xlsx")
##t1= flextable(t1)
t1 <- t1[-1, ]
t1 = flextable::as_flextable(t1,show_coltype = F, max_row = 40)
t1 = align(t1,align ="center", part = "all")
t1 <- align(t1, align = "left", part = "body", j = 1)
t1 <- set_header_labels(
  t1,
  Behavior = "Behavior",
  n_ct = "n", beta_ct = "β (95%CI)", pval_ct = "p-value",
  n_gmd = "n", beta_gmd = "β (95%CI)", pval_gmd = "p-value"
)
t1 <- colformat_num(
  t1, 
  j = c("pval_ct", "pval_gmd"), 
  digits = 2
)
t1 <- add_header_row(
  t1,
  values = c("", "Thickness/volume signature ", "Gray matter mean diffusivity signature "),
  colwidths = c(1, 3, 3)
)
t1 = add_footer_lines(t1 ,"For each behavior, independent models were constructed in which the isometric log-ratio coordinates of the movement behaviors were included as predictor variables. Models were adjusted for age and education. The table reports the results for the coordinate of the dominant behavior relative to the other behaviors. Abbreviations: 95%CI: 95% confidence interval. β: Unstandardized beta coefficients indicate how much the outcome changes for a one-unit increase in the respective ILR coordinate. This reflects a proportional increase in the dominant behavior relative to the rest of behaviors.")
t1 <- padding(t1, i=c(2:5,7:10,12:15,17:20,22:25), j=1, padding.left=20) ##i=Variable and j=Colum
t1 <- bold(t1, i = c(1,6,11,16,21), j = 1) ##Negrita words
set_caption(t1, caption = "")
```

##Figure S1.Correlation matrix

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.align="center"}  
#| echo: false 
#| fig-cap: "Figure S1.Pearson correlations between cognitive outcomes and AD signatures. Color bar represents the strength of the correlation as r values. The darker blue the color, the stronger the positive correlation between variables, and the darker red the color, the stronger the negative correlation between variables. Blank spaces represent non – significant correlations. Higher values of the gray matter mean diffusivity (GMMD) signature indicate greater microstructural brain disruption (worse brain integrity), whereas higher cortical thickness/volume signature values indicate better structural integrity."

knitr::include_graphics("C:/Users/Beatr/Desktop/Profith/Agueda/Proyectos_R/Acc_script/processed_data/fig_correlation.tiff")
```
